newsitem.title: USA: World Bank mulls making first South Africa loan.
newsitem.headline: World Bank mulls making first South Africa loan.

text.p: The World Bank is discussing making its first loan to South Africa after being approached by the government there, a Bank official said on Wednesday.
The loan, which would be on the order of $50 to $60 million, would be targetted at small and medium-sized companies, Bank Vice President Callisto Madavo said.
He told reporters that it is those types of companies that have proven successful in other countries in cracking export markets and thus creating jobs at home.
A decision on the loan could come in few months.
World Bank President James Wolfensohn is expected to discuss the loan and other issues in an upcoming visit to South Africa.
The trip, which will take place from February 8 to 16, will also take Wolfensohn to Senegal, Ghana and Mozambique.
Wolfensohn told reporters that the World Bank has not lent any money yet to South Africa because the country has access to other funding and has not been interested.
"It's been their choice," he said. "They don't want any strings tied," he added, referring to the conditions that the Bank places on its loans.
